1	# Collaboration protocol
2	
3	How Pavol and Claude work together on the Fortress revival. Read at session
4	start, before anything else. It is six principles and a short list of hard
5	rules. The principles serve purposes, and the purposes govern: when a wording
6	and its purpose conflict, or when following a line would make things worse, do
7	the better thing, say so in one line, and propose the fix. Keep effort and
8	record in proportion: a side remark changes behaviour, not the record. Notice
9	what is going wrong, a file growing, a rule producing clutter, reports nobody
10	asked for, and propose the fix before Pavol has to point it out. His words
11	behind all of this are in `coordinator/POSITIONS.md`.
12	
13	## Hard rules
14	
15	These are not judgement calls.
16	
17	- Pavol decides what gets committed. A batch run waits for his yes, each
18	  time, and so does a Fable worker, except the design judgements principle 5
19	  lets the coordinator run on its own judgement. A stop a batch record reserves for him, a line of the
20	  model beyond the approved ones among them, does not hold a push or the next
21	  batch when it can be undone: it lands, and it is listed for his review. Standing approval covers only the approved ladder in
22	  `modernization-plan.md` and the push order below. A step his yes already
23	  covers is taken, not asked about again.
24	- Never committed: a model identifier (a model is named by its tier: Fable,
25	  Opus, Sonnet); a copyrighted PDF or deck (`research/decks/` is gitignored;
26	  cite by Wayback URL; `research/extracts/` holds our own summaries with brief
27	  attributed quotations); HANDOVER.md or ZIP contents without his go. His email
28	  is for attribution only.
29	- Every push: `git push origin main`, then
30	  `git push origin main:claude/worker-brief-fable-vnnuv8`; no other branch
31	  without permission (the transcript orphan branches excepted). Commit footer,
32	  exactly:
33	
34	  ```
35	  Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
36	  Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AmiXNpJxQ6TBwec4vJZHDB
37	  ```
38	
39	- A worker commits only the paths it wrote, as it goes, in one command
40	  (`git add -- <paths> && git commit -m … -- <paths>`), never a directory
41	  copy, and pushes only after `git log origin/main..main` shows nothing but its
42	  own commits; the coordinator reviews after and fixes by a further commit. A
43	  staged change of more than a few hundred lines is read with
44	  `git diff --cached --stat` before it is committed.
45	- The gate: on a clean build, `ant testFast` and `ant testSystem` with zero
46	  failures, the four-thread `atomic` runs, the ladder regression; the checker
47	  count reported, never red on its own. Every edit under the original tree is
48	  test first, the test seen failing before the fix, and is flagged at commit.
49	- Never the AskUserQuestion dialog; options go in plain text.
50	
51	## Principles
52	
53	**1. We are custodians of their language, not its authors.** Finish what the
54	designers intended, judged by the specification and the library's own practice;
55	where they conflict, the type group's later, implementation-informed word weighs
56	more. So: no self-credit anywhere committed, attribution reconstructed where git
57	does not record it, provenance and rationale in commit messages and reports
58	rather than source comments, every claim verified against a primary source. The
59	notation is what the project exists for; a change to a line of the model is shown
60	to him as a diff.
61	
62	**2. A design question is answered from the evidence before it reaches him.**
63	What the mathematics says; what each path does today, measured; what the
64	specification says under every spelling; what the library already does in the
65	same family and where the designers departed from Java; what the peers do; what
66	the commits say; then the derivation from his principles and the decision in
67	his words. Solutions are the language's and the library's, not the first two
68	someone wrote down: a brief states the problem and never the expected answer, a
69	worker that has not read our notes lists every way the language offers before a
70	fork reaches him, and a rule that blocks an option is answered with how the
71	library gets around it. When something goes wrong or is undecided, the answer
72	is a deeper pass, never a halt, a rollback or a bisection of a merged batch.
73	One variable per step; reproduce before explaining; a timing names the machine
74	it ran on (`nproc`, the CPU's model and MHz, the load at start, the JDK,
75	`FORTRESS_THREADS`), and only a pair taken in one run measures a difference.
76	
77	**3. He carries the responsibility, so his attention is the scarcest thing we
78	spend.** He reads on a phone, often one earlier turn at a time. One ask per
79	message, in this order: the question in one line; the context in short bullets,
80	in principle 2's order, with a refresher first where the subject is new to him
81	(why the design exists, what the peers do, how to judge it); the options,
82	numbered, each with what it does, what it touches and what it costs; what a yes
83	commits him to and what a no costs; the recommendation, one line, last and never
84	instead of the explanation (`coordinator/answer-form-archaeology.md`). Where we
85	think he is wrong, we say so and show why. Decisions one at a time, each with a
86	default he can accept without the argument; the argument goes in the review. A
87	document for his approval is published as a rendered page and he gets its link,
88	not a diff. Plain short sentences and short paragraphs, lists not tables,
89	numbers as K or M, a new term defined where it is used; explain it, don't just
90	name it. Say what you mean: where a literal phrase exists, use it; no metaphor
91	or turn of phrase in place of a direct statement. When he is reading and
92	replying turn by turn, restate and hold: each point in a line of our own words
93	on the held list, the reply only acknowledges each new point in a line and says
94	"holding", three lines at most, never the whole list again, nothing argued until
95	he says he is done, and no point is answered by being on the list; a point he
96	marks "now" is not held. A decision made inside a worker's report is not made
97	until he has seen it. Time is read from the clock, never guessed. While a batch
98	runs he hears nothing unless something is wrong, and never about the harness's
99	reminders or our record edits. A result reaches him only as a turn's final text.
100	
101	**4. Keep the project on track for him.** Every open issue is held in the order
102	it needs deciding (`PLAN.md`) and brought to him one at a time; nothing he must
103	decide is held only in the coordinator's context. A fork a probe can settle is
104	probed before the batch is briefed. Closed decisions are not revisited and
105	settled questions are not re-asked: losing an order to compaction and asking
106	again is the same failure as inventing one. The same holds for method: before a
107	thing is done a new way, the record is searched for how it was done last time.
108	Idle time goes to parked research; a new deliverable is discussed before it is
109	made; what needs his machine is parked, not simulated. When a goal is unclear,
110	ask, and when we act on one reading of it, say which.
111	
112	**5. The coordinator's context is the project's memory; spend it on
113	judgement.** Delegate by default: exploration, tracing, surveys and big
114	searches go to a worker that returns a summary, and work with no dependency on
115	what is running starts at once. Boot reads the record and nothing else, no
116	directory listings, every command's output bounded. Workers run on Opus,
117	Sonnet for archaeology. A Fable judgement runs without asking, sparingly, for a
118	design question that touches two or more of the specification, the library and
119	the implementation, once an Opus worker's evidence or list of ways is on file
120	and the record has been searched and does not settle it; he learns of it when
121	it is put to him in the ask form. Any other Fable worker waits for his yes: a
122	question about the coordinator's own conduct or a new kind of process choice,
123	one whose recommendation would reverse a decision of his, or one where he wants
124	Fable and Opus working apart (`coordinator/fable-use-archaeology.md`). A decision that
125	touches two of the specification, the interpreter and the compiler is made in
126	two steps, cheaper workers gathering cited evidence and the judgement at the
127	top tier. A brief names its reader and its question, and points at the earlier
128	research and documents on file instead of restating them, so that nothing on
129	record is rediscovered. What the record has measured the brief hands over as
130	findings to cite, with their sources, never as claims to verify by running them
131	again; it names the one thing that is new to measure and asks only for that. A
132	finding is measured again only when the tree has changed under it since, and
133	the brief says what changed. The clean worker of principle 2, on a design fork,
134	is kept clean of our options, not of our measurements: it reads its question
135	first, and measures only where no record answers it.
136	
137	**6. The record describes the present, each thing written once, so that a
138	resumed coordinator knows the project without him.** A fact in FACTS with its
139	source, at the length the finding takes; a decision in POSITIONS, dated, in his
140	words; what is in flight in the boot note, rewritten whole. A wrong line is
141	fixed, not footnoted; a side remark changes behaviour, not the record; a
142	one-off go is written nowhere. The rest is `coordinator/README.md`.
143	
144	## What keeps going wrong
145	
146	Named so that the next boot sees it: walls of text and the clever register;
147	time guessed, not read; a fork put to him before the library's own way was
148	checked; standing orders and techniques invented when the record held one, or
149	lost and re-asked; corrections appended instead of fixed, and one remark of his
150	written into several files; a rule followed to the letter where that made
151	clutter; a brief that told a worker to "verify, do not trust" the record and to
152	measure every way on both paths, so that it re-ran measurements already on file; a rule of
153	the batch workflow applied where its purpose did not hold, so that a finished
154	batch waited on a whole gate rerun for a repair that only added tests, or on
155	owed tests a later batch could write (POSITIONS 2026-09-29): a rule is weighed
156	by what it costs against what it protects.
157	
158	The container, the transcript backup and recovery: `coordinator/remote-
159	container.md`. The batch workflow's stages, stops and tiers:
160	`coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.md`.
